claim: Round 6 (R6-10, VAT-r5-02) gave a public note in a picture its form: §11.2's `ExportOpts.pins` (base l. 16323–16329) 'each public note a numbered marker at its thing's anchor … numbered from 1 … the numbers keyed on §9.5's separate legend sheet to the pin's label and note and to the public note's text; a public note on a thing the export's knowledge withholds left out', and §9.5 (l. 15168–15169) adds the public notes to its *Annotation layer* ('numbered markers and a separate legend sheet'); the canon's round-6 ruling says the same. A note's words now reach a picture only on the legend sheet. V08's players' view still promises the players the notes: §3.14 (2) (l. 2299–2301) 'Every picture is drawn with … the document's public notes, view pins and annotation layer (§2.9 view state, §9.5)'; §5.3's *Notes and pins in pictures* (l. 3110–3113) 'the players see the public ones in their pictures'; T-V8-41 (l. 3308) 'public notes and view pins are drawn, private ones never'. The set has no carrier for the sheet: `PartyPictureSet` (l. 377–383) holds `levels` (PNG tiles), `svg` and `gazetteer`, `drawDigest` hashes those alone, `putPartyPictures` stores only that, the player's viewer (§3.14 (4), l. 2319–2322) shows the tiles and a caption, and the party gazetteer holds places, not notes. A player gets numbered markers with no text. Two builders differ: one invents a legend member the record, the digest and the viewer lack; one draws the note text on the tiles against §11.2; one leaves the notes out against V08 §5.3 and T-V8-41. §5.3's bullet also says every picture draws the notes, where §11.2 draws them 'never in a picture unless asked' (`pins` default false), and it does not say that a party render always asks. The subject is shared by rendering (§9.5, §11.2), V08 (the party set, `exportPicture`) and V09 (the Picture tab's 'pins and public notes'); the agreement matrix has no row for it.
required_change: V08. (1) `PartyPictureSet` (l. 381), after `gazetteer: Uint8Array /* … */;` add `legend: Uint8Array /* §9.5's legend sheet of the set's annotation layer — each numbered view pin's label and note and each numbered public note's text, numbered as §11.2's ExportOpts.pins numbers the markers on the tiles and the SVG — under the party key, an SVG inert by §11.1's bar; an empty sheet when the set draws no marker */;` and in `drawDigest`'s comment 'the gazetteer's bytes and `week`' → 'the gazetteer's and the legend's bytes and `week`'. (2) §3.14 (2), the closing clause: 'the document's public notes, view pins and annotation layer (§2.9 view state, §9.5) and never a private note or a DM-only pin.' → 'the document's view pins and public notes as §9.5's annotation layer — every party render passes `ExportOpts.pins` true, so each is a numbered marker on the tiles and the SVG, a note on a place the party key withholds left out (§11.2's `ExportOpts.pins`), keyed on the set's legend sheet (`legend`, drawn by the same render) — and never a private note or a DM-only pin.' (3) §3.14 (4): after 'the caption `host.party.asOf` (the set's `week`; V08 §5.1's table)' add ', the set's legend sheet (`legend`) below the tiles when it keys any marker'. (4) §5.3's *Notes and pins in pictures*: 'A picture draws the document's public notes and view pins and the annotation layer (§2.9 view state, §9.5) under its key;' → 'A picture draws the document's view pins and public notes as §9.5's annotation layer — numbered markers keyed on its legend sheet — when its `ExportOpts.pins` asks (§11.2; every party render asks, V08 §3.14 (2)), under its key, a note on a thing the key withholds left out;'. (5) T-V8-41: 'public notes and view pins are drawn, private ones never' → 'public notes and view pins are drawn as numbered markers keyed on the set's legend sheet (`legend`), a public note on a place the party key withholds left out, private ones never'. One fix with VAH-r6-02.

claim: V08 §3.14 (5) (l. 2326–2331) says of 'See what the players see': 'So the DM sees in the live frame exactly what the next party set will show'. T-V8-41 (l. 3308) asserts it: 'with "See what the players see" on, the frame's city band equals the party set's z0 picture at the same head (a pixel diff, both drawn with the fixed sun)'. Since round 6 the two cannot be equal on any document holding a view pin or a public note. The party set draws each view pin as 'a numbered marker in its colour at its point' and each public note as 'a numbered marker at its thing's anchor' (§11.2's `ExportOpts.pins`, base l. 16323–16329; §9.5 l. 15168). The live frame draws 'pins as markers with their colour; notes in panels' (V09's entity table, l. 4171; §4.19's Notes and Pins rows, l. 2907–2908): unnumbered pins and no note marker. T-V8-41's own fixture holds both (the same bar asserts 'public notes and view pins are drawn'), so its pixel diff cannot pass as written. Two builders differ: one draws the annotation layer in the frame while the toggle is on (a canvas mode V09 does not define), one runs the diff only on a fixture with no pin or note. Before round 6, §11.2 drew pins 'as the view draws them', so the frame and the set could agree.
required_change: V08. (1) §3.14 (5): 'So the DM sees in the live frame exactly what the next party set will show;' → 'So the DM sees in the live frame exactly what the next party set will show but its annotation layer — the view pins and public notes the set draws as numbered markers keyed on its legend sheet (§11.2's `ExportOpts.pins`), which the frame shows as V09 §4.19 does —;'. (2) T-V8-41: 'the frame's city band equals the party set's z0 picture at the same head (a pixel diff, both drawn with the fixed sun)' → 'the frame's city band equals the party set's z0 picture at the same head (a pixel diff, both drawn with the fixed sun, on the fixture's copy holding no view pin and no public note — the set's numbered markers being the annotation layer the frame does not draw, §11.2's `ExportOpts.pins`)'. One fix with VAH-r6-01.

claim: R6-03 step 2 leaves uncarried, with a late calamity, "a condition naming it" (§4.11 *The clock* (4) l. 8531; V08 §3.6 (3) l. 1874, §3.2 l. 1530, §3.6 (4) l. 1927–1928, §3.17 row l. 2702, T-V8-49 (g)). A SettlementForge condition names no calamity: `activeConditions[]` carries `id`, `archetype`, `label`, `severity`, `severityBand`, `status`, `triggeredAt.tick`, `triggeredAt.sourceEventType`, `duration` (V08 l. 665). The only link is V08 §3.16 (7) (d)'s week rule over carried calamities: "the carried calamity whose week equals its `triggeredAt.tick`, else … the latest carried calamity in the 52 weeks up to its `sinceWeek`". Builders differ: exact week only, (d)'s whole rule with the deferred calamity counted carried, or label matching. A `reconstruction` condition raised a week after the calamity, in a town with an earlier carried calamity within 52 weeks, is carried by the first build and by (d) linked to the earlier calamity, so its disaster look stands on the wrong districts (V08 §3.16 (7) (b); §10.2 (d)) until the next absorb past `W₀` re-links it, a silent wrong look; T-V8-49 (g)'s "condition naming it" fixture fits whichever reading its author takes.
required_change: 1. V08 §3.16 (7) (d), after "with none it carries no calamity.", add: "A condition **names** a calamity when this link would give it that calamity were it carried — its `triggeredAt.tick` at the calamity's week, else the calamity the latest in the 52 weeks up to the condition's `sinceWeek`; so a late calamity an absorb leaves uncarried (§4.11 *The clock* (4); V08 §3.6 (3)) holds back each condition that names it, none of them carried meanwhile or linked to an earlier calamity." 2. V08 §3.6 (3): "nor a condition naming it" → "nor a condition naming it (V08 §3.16 (7) (d))". 3. END (pipeline), §4.11 *The clock* (4): "nor a condition naming it" → "nor a condition naming it (V08 §3.16 (7) (d))". 4. T-V8-49 (g) adds: "and on a copy whose binding carries an earlier calamity in the 52 weeks before the second absorb, and whose `reconstruction` condition's `triggeredAt.tick` falls the week after the late calamity's — that condition not carried by the second absorb (no disaster look on the earlier calamity's districts), and carried by the absorb past `W₀` with the calamity, its look on the late calamity's targets".

claim: VEL5-r5-03's fix split T-V8-11's tier: "nightly, SF3; the uncarried-calamity clause nightly, SF4" (the strike needs SF4's calamities into `EpochInputs`, T-V8-42). V08's other split tiers (T-V8-18, T-V8-40, T-V8-46, T-V8-53) have their later clauses named in the later milestone's exit cell (the VH row: "T-V8-40's, T-V8-46's, T-V8-53's and T-V8-18's village clauses"). SF4's exit cell — "T-V8-16, T-V8-18, …, T-V8-59, T-V8-60" — does not name T-V8-11's clause, and SF3's names T-V8-11 whole, so the milestone table schedules the clause at SF3, before its provider. A milestone cell omitting a clause its test's tier names; MINOR.
required_change: V08 ## 8's SF4 row, its exit cell: "T-V8-16, T-V8-18," → "T-V8-11's uncarried-calamity clause, T-V8-16, T-V8-18,"; and SF3's exit cell "T-V8-11," → "T-V8-11 (its uncarried-calamity clause at SF4),".
